<summary>What is a Detection Problem?</summary>

A detection problem occurs when the threat detection system either:
- **Detects potential security threats** (prompt injection, secret leak, malicious patch)
- **Fails to produce results** (agent failure, parse error)

When `continue-on-error: true` (the default), these problems produce warnings and safe outputs still proceed. When `continue-on-error: false`, they block safe outputs entirely.

issue.title: CoreCLR iOS interpreter crashes on generic type with mutually constrained type parameters
issue.body:
### Apple platform

iOS

### Framework version

net11.0-*

### Affected platform version

.NET 11.0.100-rc.2.26504.105, iOS workload 11.0.100-rc.2.26509.2

### Description

# CoreCLR iOS interpreter crashes on generic type with mutually constrained type parameters

SIGSEGV (null dereference) inside `libcoreclr` when the CoreCLR interpreter on iOS compiles a method that touches a generic type where one type parameter is constrained by another type parameter *and* by `IComparable<T>` over itself.

The type must be in a ReadyToRun-compiled assembly. In a Debug build the iOS SDK does that for NuGet package assemblies, so a package dependency is enough to trigger it.

This repro contains no application code. It only uses the .NET iOS SDK template plus ~40 lines of generic types.

## Environment

| | |
|---|---|
| .NET SDK | `11.0.100-rc.2.26504.105` (pinned by `global.json`) |
| iOS workload | `27.0.12212-net11-rc.2` (`Microsoft.iOS.Sdk.net11.0_27.0`) |
| Runtime packs | `Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime.iossimulator-arm64` `11.0.0-rc.2.26504.105` (CoreCLR) |
| Xcode | 27.0
| Host | macOS 26.6.2, Apple silicon |
| Target | iOS Simulator 27.0 (iPhone 18 Pro), `iossimulator-arm64`, Debug |

Not tested: physical devices, `ios-arm64`, Mono (`UseMonoRuntime=true`), NativeAOT, other .NET 11 previews.

## Output

Console:

```
Repro: calling Generic<Item, Position>.Run...
Fatal error.
Got a SIGSEGV while executing native code. ...
   at RangedTypes.Entry.Run()
   at ConstraintCrashRepro.AppDelegate.FinishedLaunching(UIKit.UIApplication, Foundation.NSDictionary)
   ...
```

Native stack of the faulting thread (`EXC_BAD_ACCESS`, `KERN_INVALID_ADDRESS at 0x0`):

```

 8 libcoreclr  TypeVarTypeDesc::SatisfiesConstraints(SigTypeContext*, TypeHandle, InstantiationContext const*)
 9 libcoreclr  SatisfiesClassConstraints(TypeHandle, TypeHandle, InstantiationContext const*)
10 libcoreclr  MethodTable::DoFullyLoad(Generics::RecursionGraph*, ClassLoadLevel, CUnorderedArray<TypeHandle, 40>*, int*, InstantiationContext const*)
11 libcoreclr  PushFinalLevels(TypeHandle, ClassLoadLevel, InstantiationContext const*)
12 libcoreclr  ClassLoader::LoadTypeHandleForTypeKey(...)
13 libcoreclr  ClassLoader::LoadConstructedTypeThrowing(...)
14 libcoreclr  ClassLoader::LoadGenericInstantiationThrowing(...)
15 libcoreclr  SigPointer::GetTypeHandleThrowing(...)
16 libcoreclr  CEEInfo::getCallInfo(...)
17 libcoreclr  InterpCompiler::EmitCall(...)
18 libcoreclr  InterpCompiler::GenerateCode(...)
19 libcoreclr  InterpCompiler::CompileMethod()
20 libcoreclr  CILInterp::compileMethod(...)
21 libcoreclr  UnsafeJitFunction(...)
...
27 libcoreclr  PrepareInterpreterCode(...)
28 libcoreclr  InterpExecMethod(...)
```

## The types

`RangedTypes/GenericTypes.cs`:

```csharp
public abstract class Reference : IComparable<Reference> { ... }

public interface IHasStart<TPoint> where TPoint : Reference, IComparable<TPoint>
{
	TPoint Start { get; }
}

public abstract class Generic<TRef, TPoint>
	where TRef : Reference, IHasStart<TPoint>
	where TPoint : TRef, IComparable<TPoint>   // constrained by another type parameter and by IComparable<TPoint>
{
	public string Run(TRef reference) => reference.Start.ToString() ?? "";
}

public abstract class Item : Reference, IHasStart<Position> { ... }
public class Position : Item, IComparable<Position> { ... }
public sealed class Impl : Generic<Item, Position> { ... }
```

The app calls `Impl.Instance.Run(new Position())` through a non-generic helper (`Entry.Run`). All type arguments are reference types, so the shared canonical code `Generic<__Canon, __Canon>` is used.

## Origin

Found in a large app that depends on an internal library with a type of exactly this shape
(`StandardRangedDataType<TReference, TPoint, TRange>`), where a one-line method on the generic type crashed the app as soon as it was first called in a Debug simulator build. The same assemblies ran under the previous .NET 10 / Mono setup.


### Steps to Reproduce

https://github.com/tdiehl/coreclr-ios-interpreter-repro

1. Install the SDK and workload that `global.json` pins, and boot an iOS simulator.
2. Run:

   ```sh
   ./run.sh Debug
   ```

   `run.sh` packs `RangedTypes` into `./local-feed`, builds `App` (`dotnet build -f net11.0-ios -c Debug -r iossimulator-arm64`), installs it on the booted simulator and launches it with the console attached. To target a specific simulator:
   `./run.sh Debug <name-or-udid>`.

- Release builds precompile everything and did not crash.

issue.title: [browser] HotReload functional test is built but not submitted to Helix in CI
issue.body:
### Description

`src\tests\FunctionalTests\WebAssembly\Browser\HotReload\WebAssembly.Browser.HotReload.Test.csproj` is built and archived by the Windows browser library-test job, but its archive is not selected for execution on Helix.

The intended `browseronly` archive destination is overwritten by a parent props import, placing the test under `runonly`. The Helix selectors only pick up matching `.Sample.zip` files from `runonly`, not this `.Test.zip` file. As a result, CI can successfully build this test and submit the other tests without exercising its Hot Reload checks.

### Reproduction Steps

1. Inspect scheduled runtime [build 1639485 / 20261018.1](https://dev.azure.com/dnceng-public/public/_build/results?buildId=1639485), source `ec0059c08c077e839c6eb8827c846530a891d7e2`, specifically the successful **browser-wasm windows Release LibraryTests** job.
2. Its [Build product log](https://dev.azure.com/dnceng-public/public/_apis/build/builds/1639485/logs/2097?api-version=7.1) records compilation of the exact test, generation of both delta revisions, and this archive operation at `2026-10-18T09:21:53.5051589Z`:

   ```text
   Zipping directory "...\artifacts\bin\WebAssembly.Browser.HotReload.Test\net11.0\browser-wasm\wwwroot\"
   to "...\artifacts\helix\runonly\browser.AnyCPU.Release\WebAssembly.Browser.HotReload.Test.zip".
   ```

3. Its [Send to Helix log](https://dev.azure.com/dnceng-public/public/_apis/build/builds/1639485/logs/2102?api-version=7.1) records `WasmTestOnChrome`, a normal archive wildcard of `artifacts\helix\tests\**\*.zip`, and submission of Helix job `fce0feae-fabc-47c4-b8ef-53e6fce3eec1`.
4. Inspect the [complete Helix work-item inventory](https://helix.dot.net/api/jobs/fce0feae-fabc-47c4-b8ef-53e6fce3eec1/workitems?api-version=2019-06-17). None of its 205 work items contains `WebAssembly.Browser.HotReload.Test` or `HotReload`.

The incorrect archive path is also reproducible by evaluating the project on Windows, without building it:

```powershell
.\.dotnet\dotnet.exe msbuild .\src\tests\FunctionalTests\WebAssembly\Browser\HotReload\WebAssembly.Browser.HotReload.Test.csproj -p:TargetOS=browser -p:TargetArchitecture=wasm -p:RuntimeFlavor=Mono -p:Configuration=Release -p:ContinuousIntegrationBuild=true -p:ArchiveTests=true -getProperty:TestArchiveTestsRoot,TestArchiveTestsDir,IgnoreForCI,Scenario,ExpectedExitCode
```

At `8ab789d9e8a0dcda46c77ffbe86fc006b5dcba67`, this reports `runonly\browser.AnyCPU.Release` as the effective archive directory, an empty `IgnoreForCI`, `Scenario=WasmTestOnChrome`, and `ExpectedExitCode=42`. The implicated routing props, test sources, and submission selectors are unchanged between this revision and the inspected CI revision.

### Expected behavior

The supported Windows browser CI route should submit and execute the exact HotReload functional test. Its result should confirm both delta updates and the checked sequence `OLD STRING` → `NEW STRING` → `NEWEST STRING`, with browser exit code **42** and successful XHarness completion.

The existing non-Windows CI exclusion should remain a separate concern.

### Actual behavior

The test ZIP is created under `artifacts\helix\runonly\browser.AnyCPU.Release`, but no selector includes it in the inspected Helix job. There is no execution result for this test; its status is **not run / N/A**, not passed. Aggregate Helix success does not establish a result for an omitted test.

This was directly verified for the route/build above, not for every historical build or pipeline.

### Regression?

Unknown when this began. No earlier known-good CI execution was established. The routing problem is present in both source revisions listed above.

### Known Workarounds

The exact test is still operational locally. On Windows, using the repository SDK and locally built Mono/browser Release runtime, the following baseline and exact-project commands succeeded at `8ab789d9e8a0dcda46c77ffbe86fc006b5dcba67`:

```powershell
.\build.cmd mono+libs -os browser -c Release -restore
.\build.cmd mono+libs -os browser -c Release -build
.\.dotnet\dotnet.exe restore .\src\tests\FunctionalTests\WebAssembly\Browser\HotReload\WebAssembly.Browser.HotReload.Test.csproj -p:TargetOS=browser -p:TargetArchitecture=wasm -p:RuntimeFlavor=Mono -p:Configuration=Release -p:InstallChromeForTests=true
.\.dotnet\dotnet.exe build --no-restore .\src\tests\FunctionalTests\WebAssembly\Browser\HotReload\WebAssembly.Browser.HotReload.Test.csproj /t:Test -p:TargetOS=browser -p:TargetArchitecture=wasm -p:RuntimeFlavor=Mono -p:Configuration=Release -p:InstallChromeForTests=true
```

The initial machine-specific PATH problem was resolved with a short process-local PATH. Baseline restore used the equivalent `eng\build.ps1` entry point through an explicit Windows PowerShell executable. No repository source changes were needed.

Actual headless Chrome/XHarness output:

```text
Apply Delta Update for ApplyUpdateReferencedAssembly.dll, revision 1
Apply Delta Update for ApplyUpdateReferencedAssembly.dll, revision 2
ret: 42
WASM EXIT 42
XHarness exit code: 0
```

### Configuration

- CI: scheduled `runtime` pipeline, definition 129, `main`, Windows host, browser-wasm, Mono, Release, `WasmTestOnChrome`.
- Inspected CI build: `1639485`, queued October 18, 2026. The Windows LibraryTests job succeeded; the overall build failed elsewhere.
- Local confirmation: Windows x64 host, browser-wasm Mono interpreter, Release, headless Chromium 155.0.8059.85, repository SDK `11.0.100-rc.1.26420.103`.

### Other information

**Cause: archive-property import order plus selection mismatch.**

- [`src\libraries\tests.proj`](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/8ab789d9e8a0dcda46c77ffbe86fc006b5dcba67/src/libraries/tests.proj#L842-L849) includes the WebAssembly `*.Test.csproj` projects when archiving the full browser test set.
- [`WebAssembly\Directory.Build.props`](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/8ab789d9e8a0dcda46c77ffbe86fc006b5dcba67/src/tests/FunctionalTests/WebAssembly/Directory.Build.props#L9-L15) assigns `TestArchiveTestsRoot` and `TestArchiveTestsDir` to `browseronly` **before** importing its parent props.
- The parent functional-test props sets `IsFunctionalTest=true` and imports [`src\libraries\Directory.Build.props`](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/8ab789d9e8a0dcda46c77ffbe86fc006b5dcba67/src/libraries/Directory.Build.props#L76-L80). That import replaces the root with `runonly` for functional tests and recomputes the directory.
- [`sendtohelix-browser.targets`](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/8ab789d9e8a0dcda46c77ffbe86fc006b5dcba67/src/libraries/sendtohelix-browser.targets#L322-L360) includes `browseronly\**\*.zip` for browser scenarios, but promotes only `runonly\**\*.Browser.*.Sample.zip` for Chrome or `runonly\**\*.Console.V8.*.Sample.zip` for V8. `WebAssembly.Browser.HotReload.Test.zip` matches neither. The normal selector covers `tests\**\*.zip`.

**Suggested remedy:** Move the existing `TestArchiveTestsRoot` and `TestArchiveTestsDir` assignments in `WebAssembly\Directory.Build.props` to after the parent import. This should restore the intended `browseronly` destination, which the browser submission selector already handles. This change has not been applied or validated; verification should check the effective archive path, inclusion of the exact work item, and its actual browser result.

Related but distinct: [#114526](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/114526) tracks the intentional Linux exclusion for deadlocks; [#118442](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/118442) concerns HotReload in the separate Wasm.Build.Tests suite.

> [!NOTE]
> This issue was prepared and filed with GitHub Copilot assistance.

comment.body:
Could we let `JsonSerializer` serialize the whole message sequence instead of manually writing the array and iterating over the arguments?

Adding this to `IpcJsonSerializerContext`, alongside the existing concrete argument-type registrations:

```csharp
[JsonSerializable(typeof(IEnumerable<object>), TypeInfoPropertyName = "MessageSequence")]
```

would allow the array-writing code and loop to become:

```csharp
JsonSerializer.Serialize(
    writer,
    args.Prepend(messageType),
    IpcJsonSerializerContext.Default.MessageSequence);
```

The concrete argument types still need their registrations, but source-generated metadata supports runtime-type dispatch for `object` elements, so NativeAOT does not require this manual loop. Using the writer overload also leaves room to construct the prefixed result without an intermediate JSON string.

### Description

Debugging interfaces on mobile platforms changing to `ICorDebug`

### Version

.NET 11

### Previous behavior

.NET runtime debugging interfaces for Apple mobile platforms were based on the
Mono soft debugger and its underlying protocols.

### New behavior

CoreCLR debugging uses the documented `ICorDebug` interfaces. This matches the
debugging interface used by other CoreCLR platforms.

### Type of breaking change

- [x] Source incompatible
- [x] Binary incompatible
- [x] Behavioral change

### Reason for change

Mono and CoreCLR use different debugger interfaces and components.

### Recommended action

- Replace Mono soft-debugger integration with `ICorDebug`.
- Follow the
  [mobile CoreCLR debugger initialization guidance](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/core/unmanaged-api/debugging/initialize-debugger-mobile)
  for the target-side component and `ICorDebug` initialization sequence.
- Microsoft's Visual Studio mobile debugger proxy is not a public debugging
protocol. The Visual Studio license doesn't allow third parties to redistribute
that proxy.

### Feature area

Debugger

### Affected APIs

Mono soft-debugger interfaces and protocols. CoreCLR debugger integrations use
`ICorDebug`.

issue.body:
### Description

Crash-reporting behavior changes on mobile platforms

Feature area: mobile runtime diagnostics.

### Version

.NET 11

### Previous behavior

Mono mobile launchers wrote managed exception text and managed stack traces to
Android logcat or the Apple device log. Fatal native crashes continued through
the Android tombstone or Apple crash-report path.

### New behavior

CoreCLR still writes the crashing thread's managed call stack to Android logcat
or the Apple console/device log. The text format differs from Mono. Mono can
print more text for a native crash, while CoreCLR uses a layout closer to other
CoreCLR platforms.

Android tombstones and Apple crash reports contain the same kinds of data as
before, but runtime module names change because `libmonosgen` is gone. The
native stack can also be shorter because CoreCLR has fewer native frames before
managed code.

CoreCLR also adds an opt-in in-process crash reporter. It can write a compact
report to Android logcat or the Apple console/device log, depending on the
platform, and a JSON report to a writable directory. Mobile CoreCLR doesn't
create binary dumps for later SOS analysis.

### Type of breaking change

- [ ] Source incompatible
- [ ] Binary incompatible
- [x] Behavioral change

### Reason for change

CoreCLR and Mono use different crash handlers and report formats.

### Recommended action

- Don't assume that Mono and CoreCLR produce the same crash files or log text.
- Update crash collection and parsing tools for CoreCLR names and JSON fields.
- Test custom native signal handlers with the CoreCLR crash reporter.

None. This change affects crash-report environment variables, files, and tools.

labels.name: repo-1d418140
labels.description: Identifies that an issue has been imported into Quest.

issue.body:
### Description

CoreCLR trace events replace Mono trace events

Feature area: mobile runtime diagnostics.

### Version

.NET 11

### Previous behavior

Mobile trace and profiler tools could request Mono events. Some tools used the
Mono-only `Microsoft-DotNETRuntimeMonoProfiler` provider for method enter and
leave tracing.

Mono EventPipe was a separate component. Mobile Release builds could leave that
component out.

### New behavior

`dotnet-trace` and `.nettrace` files remain supported.
[dotnet-dsrouter](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/core/diagnostics/dotnet-dsrouter)
can connect the mobile diagnostic port over TCP.

CoreCLR events replace the smaller set of Mono events. A provider with the same
name might still use different event IDs, data, ordering, or stack information.
CoreCLR doesn't provide the `Microsoft-DotNETRuntimeMonoProfiler` provider.

EventPipe should otherwise work in the same way for most users. CoreCLR
diagnostics are part of the mobile runtime, but diagnostics must be enabled when
the app is built. Set `EnableDiagnostics=true` to enable diagnostics.

See [Tracing .NET for Android applications](https://github.com/dotnet/android/blob/main/Documentation/guides/tracing.md)
and the
[Apple `EnableDiagnostics` build property](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/ios/building-apps/build-properties#enablediagnostics).

### Type of breaking change

- [x] Source incompatible
- [x] Binary incompatible
- [x] Behavioral change

### Reason for change

CoreCLR and Mono provide different runtime events and profiler features.

### Recommended action

- Test custom trace tools with the documented
  [runtime events](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/fundamentals/diagnostics/runtime-events)
  and
  [well-known providers](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/core/diagnostics/well-known-event-providers).
- Stop requesting `Microsoft-DotNETRuntimeMonoProfiler`.

Other (please put exact area in description textbox)

The `Microsoft-DotNETRuntimeMonoProfiler` EventPipe provider and Mono event
schemas.

issue.title: [Breaking change]: Mono embedding APIs no longer supported on mobile platforms

labels.name: repo-1d418140
labels.description: Identifies that an issue has been imported into Quest.

issue.body:
### Description

Mono embedding APIs no longer supported on mobile platforms

### Version

.NET 11

### Previous behavior

Native code could embed Mono by using Mono header files, linking to
`libmonosgen-2.0`, and calling `mono_*` APIs. These APIs exposed runtime,
domain, metadata, object, method-call, GC-handle, internal-call, thread, and
profiling features.

### New behavior

Mono embedding APIs are no longer supported. CoreCLR on mobile platforms
doesn't provide a direct replacement for the Mono embedding API.

This change doesn't affect normal P/Invoke, `LibraryImport`, Java interop, or
Objective-C interop.

### Type of breaking change

- [x] Source incompatible
- [x] Binary incompatible
- [x] Behavioral change

### Reason for change

Mono and CoreCLR use different hosting and embedding interfaces.

### Recommended action

- Follow
  [native interoperability best practices](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/standard/native-interop/best-practices).
- Use `[UnmanagedCallersOnly]` and C# function pointers for native-to-managed
  callbacks.
- Use values that have the same layout in managed and native code (blittable
  values).
- Consider moving performance-critical, chatty managed/native interfaces to a
  fully managed implementation to reduce interop overhead.

### Feature area

Interop

### Affected APIs

The Mono native embedding API, including `mono_*` functions and
`libmonosgen-2.0`.

Feature area: mobile runtime configuration.

### Previous behavior

Mono environment variables and launcher settings controlled logging, profiling,
diagnostics, GC, the interpreter, the JIT, thread suspension, assembly lookup,
and debugging.

- `MONO_LOG_*`
- `MONO_PROFILE`
- `MONO_DIAGNOSTICS`

- `MONO_GC_*`

- `MONO_DEBUG`

### Description

Code generation on mobile changes from Mono to CoreCLR

### Version

.NET 11

### Previous behavior

.NET 10 mobile apps could use the Mono JIT, Mono AOT, Mono AOT with LLVM, and the
Mono interpreter. The available modes depended on the target and build
configuration.

Some apps used the Mono interpreter for only a selected list of assemblies.
This helped those apps balance compatibility and speed.

### New behavior

.NET 11 mobile apps can use the CoreCLR JIT, ReadyToRun (R2R), and the CoreCLR
interpreter. The available modes still depend on the target and build
configuration.

R2R is an AOT technology, but it is not a new name for Mono AOT. It keeps IL
and metadata in the app and can use the JIT or interpreter when the target
allows it.

Android Release builds use CoreCLR R2R to precompile part of the app and use the
JIT for the rest. `MauiEnableFullReadyToRun=true` applies R2R to the entire app.
The app can still use the JIT at run time for dynamic behavior. Debug builds use
less R2R, so most of the app runs with the JIT.

Apple Release builds precompile the entire app with R2R and can use the
interpreter at run time for dynamic behavior. Debug builds use less R2R, so most
of the app runs with the interpreter.

[NativeAOT](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/maui/deployment/nativeaot?view=net-maui-11.0)
is another code generation option on mobile platforms. It is different from
both Mono AOT and CoreCLR R2R. Android NativeAOT is experimental in .NET 11.

### Type of breaking change

- [x] Source incompatible
- [ ] Binary incompatible
- [x] Behavioral change

### Reason for change

CoreCLR uses its own compiler and execution model. Mono AOT settings don't
control CoreCLR R2R.

### Recommended action

- Use the R2R defaults from the mobile workload.
- Don't try to translate each Mono AOT setting into an R2R setting.
- Use `MauiEnableFullReadyToRun` only after you measure the app.
- Measure startup time, speed, memory use, and app size.
- If you are considering NativeAOT, review the
  [.NET MAUI Native AOT deployment guidance](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/maui/deployment/nativeaot?view=net-maui-11.0)
  because it is a separate deployment model with different restrictions.
  Treat Android NativeAOT as experimental in .NET 11.

### Feature area

Deployment; JIT

### Affected APIs

No managed APIs are removed. The following MSBuild properties and items no
longer provide their Mono code-generation effect when the app uses CoreCLR:

- **Android:** `RunAOTCompilation`, `AotAssemblies`, `EnableLLVM`,
  `AndroidEnableProfiledAot`, `AndroidAotMode`,
  `AndroidAotAdditionalArguments`, `AndroidExtraAotOptions`,
  `@(AndroidAotProfile)`, `AndroidAotEnableLazyLoad`,
  `AndroidUseInterpreter`, `UseInterpreter`, and
  `AndroidEnableMarshalMethods`.
- **iOS, tvOS, and Mac Catalyst:** `UseInterpreter`, `MtouchInterpreter`,
  `MtouchUseLlvm`, `MtouchFloat32`, `MonoUseCompressedInterfaceBitmap`,
  `RunAotCompilation`, `AotAssemblies`, and
  `AotCompileMaxDegreeOfParallelism`.

These settings configure Mono AOT compilation, LLVM, interpreter selection,
AOT inputs, or generated marshal methods. They don't configure the CoreCLR
ReadyToRun pipeline. For the detailed migration and build-diagnostic behavior,
see
[Mono project properties no longer configure mobile apps](https://github.com/dotnet/docs/issues/56477).

- `MtouchFloat32`
- `MonoUseCompressedInterfaceBitmap`
- `RunAotCompilation`
- `AotAssemblies`
- `AotCompileMaxDegreeOfParallelism`

The Mono-specific settings don't provide their previous behavior on CoreCLR.
Some settings have no effect. Others cause a build warning or error.

`AndroidEnableMarshalMethods` can't be combined with ReadyToRun. This
combination causes build error `XA1049`.

- [x] Source incompatible
- [ ] Binary incompatible
- [x] Behavioral change

Most of these settings configure Mono components that aren't used by CoreCLR.
`AndroidEnableMarshalMethods` is included because its previous build
configuration isn't compatible with the CoreCLR ReadyToRun path.

### Recommended action

- Remove the Mono-specific settings from .NET 11 projects, or set them only for
  .NET 10.
- Don't enable `AndroidEnableMarshalMethods` in a CoreCLR ReadyToRun build.
- Retest the app's performance and memory use.

issue.title: [browser] HotReload functional test is built but not submitted to Helix in CI
issue.body:
### Description

`src\tests\FunctionalTests\WebAssembly\Browser\HotReload\WebAssembly.Browser.HotReload.Test.csproj` is built and archived by the Windows browser library-test job, but its archive is not selected for execution on Helix.

The intended `browseronly` archive destination is overwritten by a parent props import, placing the test under `runonly`. The Helix selectors only pick up matching `.Sample.zip` files from `runonly`, not this `.Test.zip` file. As a result, CI can successfully build this test and submit the other tests without exercising its Hot Reload checks.

### Reproduction Steps

1. Inspect scheduled runtime [build 1639485 / 20261018.1](https://dev.azure.com/dnceng-public/public/_build/results?buildId=1639485), source `ec0059c08c077e839c6eb8827c846530a891d7e2`, specifically the successful **browser-wasm windows Release LibraryTests** job.
2. Its [Build product log](https://dev.azure.com/dnceng-public/public/_apis/build/builds/1639485/logs/2097?api-version=7.1) records compilation of the exact test, generation of both delta revisions, and this archive operation at `2026-10-18T09:21:53.5051589Z`:

   ```text
   Zipping directory "...\artifacts\bin\WebAssembly.Browser.HotReload.Test\net11.0\browser-wasm\wwwroot\"
   to "...\artifacts\helix\runonly\browser.AnyCPU.Release\WebAssembly.Browser.HotReload.Test.zip".
   ```

3. Its [Send to Helix log](https://dev.azure.com/dnceng-public/public/_apis/build/builds/1639485/logs/2102?api-version=7.1) records `WasmTestOnChrome`, a normal archive wildcard of `artifacts\helix\tests\**\*.zip`, and submission of Helix job `fce0feae-fabc-47c4-b8ef-53e6fce3eec1`.
4. Inspect the [complete Helix work-item inventory](https://helix.dot.net/api/jobs/fce0feae-fabc-47c4-b8ef-53e6fce3eec1/workitems?api-version=2019-06-17). None of its 205 work items contains `WebAssembly.Browser.HotReload.Test` or `HotReload`.

The incorrect archive path is also reproducible by evaluating the project on Windows, without building it:

```powershell
.\.dotnet\dotnet.exe msbuild .\src\tests\FunctionalTests\WebAssembly\Browser\HotReload\WebAssembly.Browser.HotReload.Test.csproj -p:TargetOS=browser -p:TargetArchitecture=wasm -p:RuntimeFlavor=Mono -p:Configuration=Release -p:ContinuousIntegrationBuild=true -p:ArchiveTests=true -getProperty:TestArchiveTestsRoot,TestArchiveTestsDir,IgnoreForCI,Scenario,ExpectedExitCode
```

At `8ab789d9e8a0dcda46c77ffbe86fc006b5dcba67`, this reports `runonly\browser.AnyCPU.Release` as the effective archive directory, an empty `IgnoreForCI`, `Scenario=WasmTestOnChrome`, and `ExpectedExitCode=42`. The implicated routing props, test sources, and submission selectors are unchanged between this revision and the inspected CI revision.

### Expected behavior

The supported Windows browser CI route should submit and execute the exact HotReload functional test. Its result should confirm both delta updates and the checked sequence `OLD STRING` → `NEW STRING` → `NEWEST STRING`, with browser exit code **42** and successful XHarness completion.

The existing non-Windows CI exclusion should remain a separate concern.

### Actual behavior

The test ZIP is created under `artifacts\helix\runonly\browser.AnyCPU.Release`, but no selector includes it in the inspected Helix job. There is no execution result for this test; its status is **not run / N/A**, not passed. Aggregate Helix success does not establish a result for an omitted test.

This was directly verified for the route/build above, not for every historical build or pipeline.

### Regression?

Unknown when this began. No earlier known-good CI execution was established. The routing problem is present in both source revisions listed above.

### Known Workarounds

The exact test is still operational locally. On Windows, using the repository SDK and locally built Mono/browser Release runtime, the following baseline and exact-project commands succeeded at `8ab789d9e8a0dcda46c77ffbe86fc006b5dcba67`:


issue.title: [Breaking change]: CoreCLR replaces Mono runtime for .NET mobile apps

labels.name: repo-1d418140
labels.description: Identifies that an issue has been imported into Quest.

issue.body:
### Description

CoreCLR replaces Mono runtime for .NET mobile apps

### Version

.NET 11

### Previous behavior

Supported .NET 10 Android, iOS, tvOS, and Mac Catalyst projects used Mono by
default. A project could set `UseMonoRuntime=true` to select Mono.

Apps and tools could also see Mono names in runtime information, package files,
stack traces, symbols, and diagnostic events.

### New behavior

Supported .NET 11 Android, iOS, tvOS, and Mac Catalyst projects use CoreCLR.
Setting `UseMonoRuntime=true` causes build error
[NETSDK1242](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/core/tools/sdk-errors/netsdk1242).

Apps and tools can see new runtime names. For example:

- [`System.Runtime.InteropServices.RuntimeInformation.FrameworkDescription`](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.runtime.interopservices.runtimeinformation.frameworkdescription)
  reports .NET instead of Mono.
- Android packages contain CoreCLR files instead of `libmonosgen-2.0`.
- Stack traces, symbols, and diagnostic events identify CoreCLR.

### Type of breaking change

- [x] Source incompatible
- [x] Binary incompatible
- [x] Behavioral change

### Reason for change

.NET 11 mobile workloads use CoreCLR as their supported runtime.

### Recommended action

- Remove `UseMonoRuntime=true` from .NET 11 projects.
- If an app must use Mono, keep it on .NET 10.
- Update tools that look for Mono package files, symbols, stack frames, or
  diagnostic names.
- Don't add code that checks whether the runtime is Mono or CoreCLR. Check for
  the feature that the app needs instead.

### Feature area

SDK; Deployment

### Affected APIs

[`System.Runtime.InteropServices.RuntimeInformation.FrameworkDescription`](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.runtime.interopservices.runtimeinformation.frameworkdescription)
reports .NET instead of Mono.

issue.title: Uploaded-file downloads fail on relative Helix redirects and surface a misleading JSON parsing error
issue.body:
## Problem

Uploaded-file operations fail even though `helix_files` lists valid absolute blob URLs and the files are readable directly. This affects `helix_parse_uploaded_trx`, uploaded-file `helix_search`, and the shared work-item download path.

Observed with `Lewing.Helix.Mcp` 0.11.0 (`e713995ea5070429f4aee44cfbdbe35dd632d37a`) and `Microsoft.DotNet.Helix.Client` 11.0.0-beta.26325.102.

## Reproduction

Call `helix_parse_uploaded_trx` with:

```json
{"jobId":"c2a682b0-bb4b-46c8-8ac5-8077cd721f78","workItem":"Regression_o_3","maxResults":10}
```

Actual result:

```text
Unexpected error during parse test results: Unexpected character encountered while parsing value: <. Path '', line 0, position 0.
```

The same work item's `helix_files` call succeeds and lists `testResults.xml`. Its absolute blob URL works:

```text
https://helixr1107v0xdeko0k025g8.blob.core.windows.net/dotnet-runtime-refs-pull-135167-merge-c2a682b0bb4b46c88a/Regression_o_3/1/testResults.xml?helixlogtype=result
```

The complete document is 30,188 bytes of well-formed xUnit XML, with an `assemblies` root and 168 test elements. This is not an XML parsing failure.

## Cause and evidence

The SDK downloads through:

```text
https://helix.dot.net/api/2019-06-17/jobs/c2a682b0-bb4b-46c8-8ac5-8077cd721f78/workitems/Regression_o_3/files/testResults.xml
```

On October 19, 2026 this returned HTTP 302 with:

```text
Location: /dotnet-runtime-refs-pull-135167-merge-c2a682b0bb4b46c88a/Regression_o_3/1/testResults.xml
```

The redirect omits the blob-storage hostname. Following it stays on `helix.dot.net` and returns HTTP 404 with `Content-Type: text/html; charset=utf-8` and a body beginning `<!DOCTYPE html>`.

The SDK's failure handler then attempts to deserialize that HTML as JSON, hiding the HTTP failure:

```text
Newtonsoft.Json.JsonReaderException: Unexpected character encountered while parsing value: <.
  at Microsoft.DotNet.Helix.Client.WorkItem.OnGetFileFailed(...) in generated-code/WorkItem.cs:line 140
  at Microsoft.DotNet.Helix.Client.WorkItem.GetFileAsync(...) in generated-code/WorkItem.cs:line 116
  at HelixTool.Core.Helix.HelixApiClient.ClassifyAsync(...)
  at HelixTool.Core.Helix.HelixService.DownloadFilesAsync(...)
  at HelixTool.Core.Helix.HelixService.ParseTrxResultsAsync(...)
```

A second reproduction uses uploaded-file `helix_search`:

```json
{"jobId":"d5621f4f-70e8-438f-a834-1a7e47a77b86","workItem":"System.Net.WebSockets.Client.Tests","fileName":"net.dot.System.Net.WebSockets.Client.Tests.log","pattern":"START","maxMatches":5,"contextLines":1}
```

It returns the same JSON error, and its download endpoint has the same relative-redirect problem. Its absolute blob URL from file listing works. Console-only search is unaffected.

## Expected behavior / proposed correction

Download uploaded files from the absolute `IWorkItemFile.Link` returned by `ListFiles`, rather than the SDK file endpoint with the broken redirect. Apply this in the shared download implementation so CLI and MCP downloads, file-content search, and result parsing all benefit. Preserve artifact caching, streaming, cancellation, and normal HTTP error reporting.

Add deterministic regression coverage for successful listed-link downloads and HTTP failures, plus the search and test-result parsing paths. The Helix service redirect and SDK non-JSON error handling could also be corrected upstream, but hlx can avoid this broken endpoint independently.

issue.body:

## Incident

- Run: https://github.com/dotnet/xharness/actions/runs/38988138819
- Agent job: https://github.com/dotnet/xharness/actions/runs/38988138819/job/117264440196

## Analysis

Run https://github.com/dotnet/xharness/actions/runs/38988138819 selected runtime build `1637751`. The agent job at https://github.com/dotnet/xharness/actions/runs/38988138819/job/117264440196 found 48 successful Helix submissions, traversed 16, and then emitted `missing_data` because the remaining submissions and work-item consoles were unevaluated.

Current upstream source makes the growth deterministic:

- `.github/workflows/runtime-failure-observer.agent.md:198` requires one selected build to be processed completely before the next build.
- `.github/workflows/runtime-failure-observer.agent.md:214` requires every successful Helix submission under a failed monitor task to be inspected.
- `.github/workflows/runtime-failure-observer.agent.md:316` makes the selected timeline, submission logs, work-item responses, and candidate consoles required evidence.

The prior occurrence in #1782 stopped on 47 successful submissions; this occurrence stopped on 48. That recurrence supports traversal scope as the limiting factor rather than a malformed response or unavailable tool.

Existing-work review:

- Open PR #1783 adds a terminal safe-output invariant. This occurrence already invoked `missing_data`, so that change does not resolve the capacity problem.
- Merged PR #1785 upgraded gh-aw and removed the custom failure post-step, but it did not change the observer's evidence traversal requirements.

issue.body:
https://github.com/user-3eed6aa8/repo-6fd065e1/issues/1782

## Incident

- Run: https://github.com/dotnet/xharness/actions/runs/38564313045
- Agent job: https://github.com/dotnet/xharness/actions/runs/38564313045/job/115853354963
- Detection Runs occurrence: https://github.com/dotnet/xharness/issues/1697#issuecomment-6168471818

The agent completed successfully but produced no safe-output items. Its final response said:

> I’m unable to complete the required evidence traversal within this run: build `1634493` contains 47 independent successful Helix submissions that each require full job/work-item/console inspection before any candidate can be safely classified.

## Root cause

The workflow defined `missing_data` for unavailable or malformed evidence, but it did not explicitly require a terminal safe-output when the agent abandoned required traversal because the remaining scope was too large. Add a terminal-output invariant to the observer prompt:

- prose alone is never a valid completion;
- every run must invoke at least one terminal safe-output; and
- unfinished required traversal must emit `missing_data` with the uninspected scope.

This preserves the existing behavior for successful no-op scans and candidate PRs while making incomplete scans observable.

issue.title: SIGSEGV in GC stack walk (MethodDesc::GetSig) with mixed interpreter/ReadyToRun execution on iOS (.NET   11 RC1)
issue.body:
### Description

On .NET 11 RC1 for iOS (CoreCLR), a Release build crashes with `EXC_BAD_ACCESS (SIGSEGV)` inside the GC a few seconds after launch. Reproduced on **both the simulator (`iossimulator-arm64`) and a physical device (`ios-arm64`)**. Setting `PublishReadyToRun=false` avoids it.

The crash is in `MethodDesc::GetSig`, reached from `TransitionFrame::PromoteCallerStack` while the GC scans stack roots during `mark_phase`. The GC reads what it believes is a `MethodDesc*` out of a `TransitionFrame` and dereferences it.

**The value it dereferences is not a pointer — it is executable code.** The faulting address is `0xa9025bf5a90153f9`; the value read from the frame is `0xa9025bf5a90153f3`. Decoded as AArch64, those 8 bytes are two consecutive instructions:

```
a9025bf5    stp x21, x22, [sp, #32]
a90153f9    stp x25, x20, [sp, #16]
```

That is a function prologue. The stack walker did not read a corrupted `MethodDesc` — it misidentified the frame layout and read bytes out of the code stream.

The crashing thread's stack interleaves CoreCLR interpreter frames with ReadyToRun frames:

```
InterpExecMethod / ExecuteInterpretedMethod / InterpreterStubRetVoid   <- interpreter
<app>.r2r                                                              <- ReadyToRun
CallJittedMethodRetVoid / InvokeCalliStub
```

The main thread shows ~19 levels of nested interpreter↔R2R recursion at the point of the crash.

### Observed matrix

| Configuration | `PublishReadyToRun` | r2r framework in bundle | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| Debug, simulator | `true` (SDK default) | yes | stable |
| Release, simulator | `true` (SDK default) | yes | **SIGSEGV ~3s after launch** |
| Release, device | `true` (SDK default) | yes | **SIGSEGV ~7s after launch** |
| Release, simulator | `false` | no | stable (75s+) |
| Release, device | `false` | no | stable (10 min) |

I have not isolated what differs between the stable Debug build and the crashing Release build — both ship an r2r framework and both have `PublishReadyToRun=true`. Toggling `PublishReadyToRun` in Release is the only change I found that reliably flips the outcome.

`PublishReadyToRun` is defaulted to `true` by the iOS SDK for all CoreCLR builds — it is not an opt-in and not Release-specific (`Xamarin.Shared.Sdk.props:302`):

```xml
<!-- ReadyToRun configuration for CoreCLR -->
<PropertyGroup Condition="'$(UseMonoRuntime)' == 'false' And '$(_PlatformName)' != 'macOS' And '$(_UseNativeAot)' != 'true'">
  <PublishReadyToRun Condition="'$(PublishReadyToRun)' == ''">true</PublishReadyToRun>
  <PublishReadyToRunComposite Condition="... ">true</PublishReadyToRunComposite>
  <PublishReadyToRunContainerFormat Condition="... ">macho</PublishReadyToRunContainerFormat>
```

### Environment

| | |
|---|---|
| SDK | `11.0.100-rc.1.26425.128` |
| Workload set | `11.0.100-rc.1.26460.1` |
| iOS workload manifest | `26.5.12194-net11-rc.1/11.0.100-rc.1` |
| TFM | `net11.0-ios` |
| RIDs affected | `iossimulator-arm64` **and** `ios-arm64` |
| Host | macOS 26.6.2 (25G83), Mac mini M1 |
| Xcode | 26.6 (17F113) |
| Simulator | iPhone 17, iOS 26.4.1 |
| Device | iPad, iOS 26.6.1 |

App scale: ~295 managed assemblies (Avalonia + ReactiveUI + MAUI Essentials).

Relevant Release configuration:

```xml
<MtouchLink>SdkOnly</MtouchLink>
<!-- PublishReadyToRun is NOT set in the project; the iOS SDK defaults it to true -->
```

Resolved: `Registrar=trimmable-static`, `PublishReadyToRun=true`, `PublishReadyToRunComposite=true`, `PublishReadyToRunContainerFormat=macho`, `UseMonoRuntime=false`, `AOTCompiler=` (empty).

The project also sets `MtouchInterpreter=-all` and `EnableSGenConc=true`, but the SDK reports both as having no effect under CoreCLR, so they should not be relevant:

```
warning : The property 'MtouchInterpreter' has no effect when not using the Mono runtime
          (for instance when using CoreCLR).
warning : The property 'EnableSGenConc' has no effect when not using the Mono runtime ...
```

### Faulting stack (thread 20, simulator)

```
libcoreclr  MethodDesc::GetSig(unsigned char const**, unsigned int*) + 40
libcoreclr  MethodDesc::GetSignature() + 40
libcoreclr  TransitionFrame::PromoteCallerStack(void (*)(Object**, ScanContext*, unsigned int), ScanContext*) + 76
libcoreclr  GcStackCrawlCallBack(CrawlFrame*, void*) + 508
libcoreclr  Thread::MakeStackwalkerCallback(...) + 116
libcoreclr  Thread::StackWalkFramesEx(...) + 404
libcoreclr  Thread::StackWalkFrames(...) + 180
libcoreclr  ScanStackRoots(Thread*, ...) + 256
libcoreclr  GCToEEInterface::GcScanRoots(...) + 260
libcoreclr  WKS::gc_heap::mark_phase(int) + 552
libcoreclr  WKS::gc_heap::gc1() + 444
libcoreclr  WKS::gc_heap::garbage_collect(int) + 1156
libcoreclr  WKS::GCHeap::GarbageCollectGeneration(unsigned int, gc_reason) + 716
libcoreclr  WKS::gc_heap::trigger_gc_for_alloc(...) + 176
libcoreclr  WKS::gc_heap::try_allocate_more_space(...) + 692
libcoreclr  WKS::GCHeap::Alloc(gc_alloc_context*, unsigned long, unsigned int) + 124
libcoreclr  Alloc(ee_alloc_context*, unsigned long, GC_ALLOC_FLAGS) + 324
libcoreclr  AllocateSzArray(MethodTable*, int, GC_ALLOC_FLAGS) + 656
libcoreclr  RhpGcAlloc + 200
libcoreclr  RhpNewVariableSizeObject + 48
<app>.r2r   (allocation site in ReadyToRun code)
...
libcoreclr  InvokeUnmanagedCalliWithTransition(...)
libcoreclr  InterpExecMethod(...)
libcoreclr  ExecuteInterpretedMethod + 480
```

Register state at the fault:

```
x0:  0xa9025bf5a90153f3     x22: 0xa9025bf5a90153f3
far: 0xa9025bf5a90153f9     esr: 0x92000004 (Data Abort) byte read Translation fault
pc:  MethodDesc::GetSig + 40
Exception Subtype: KERN_INVALID_ADDRESS at 0xa9025bf5a90153f9
                   (possible pointer authentication failure)
```

On the device the app terminates identically (`Got a SIGSEGV while executing native code` / `App terminated due to signal 11`) about 7 seconds after launch. I did not pull the device crash report, so the symbolicated stack above is from the simulator.

### Repro

1. Build a reasonably large `net11.0-ios` CoreCLR app in Release with `MtouchLink=SdkOnly`, leaving `PublishReadyToRun` unset so the iOS SDK default (`true`) applies.
2. Launch on an arm64 simulator or a device.
3. The app starts and renders normally, then dies with SIGSEGV on the first GC that walks one of these frames — ~3s on the simulator, ~7s on device, reproducible every time.

I was not able to reduce this to a minimal project; it reproduces consistently in the full app but I do not know which code path allocates at the critical moment.

### Workaround

```xml
<PublishReadyToRun>false</PublishReadyToRun>
```

Verified stable: 75s+ on the simulator and 10 minutes on a physical device, where the default configuration crashed within seconds every time.

The workaround is expensive. With R2R off and no Mono AOT in play (`AOTCompiler=` is empty), the device IPA ships **no precompiled managed code at all** — 295 managed assemblies plus `libcoreclr.framework`, no r2r framework. Since iOS prohibits JIT on device, the app then runs fully interpreted.

### Notes

- After the fault, the signal handler ran `EEPolicy::LogManagedCallstackForSignal` on thread 0, which itself faulted in `TypeString::AppendMethodImpl` — presumably on the same bad `MethodDesc`. Thread 0's reported stack is therefore the logging path, not its original state.
